description: Brali Research Watch review batch for 2026-09-12. Two recent full-text systematic reviews were checked against existing Brali content. A 2026 meta-analysis of controlled urban-green experiments provides a useful refinement for the existing 10-minute stress-walk hack; a 2025 RCT meta-analysis of urban green exercise supports the direction while also showing why subgroup-derived 'optimal' duration and frequency should not become a prescription. No duplicate hack is created. Discovery metadata remains separate from the Evidence Decisions.

research_candidates.title: Mental health benefits of urban green—A systematic review and meta-analysis of 56 pre-post control experiments
research_candidates.review_notes: Full publisher article reviewed, not just discovery metadata. The synthesis meta-analysed 107 pre-post controlled measurements from 56 experiments and quasi-experiments across state anxiety, positive and negative mood, self-reported stress, depression, restoration, attention and working memory. About half of study samples were majority university students; studies were concentrated in Europe and North America. The pooled self-reported stress effect was 0.40 (95% CI 0.16 to 0.64; k=11), but the 95% prediction interval crossed zero and trim-and-fill reduced the estimate to 0.19. Attention showed a positive pooled effect, whereas working memory was not statistically significant (0.22, 95% CI -0.12 to 0.56). For outcomes where duration could be explored, the authors found no clear dose-response pattern. The review included both in-situ and mediated/virtual forms of urban nature; in-situ evidence is therefore more directly relevant to a walking route than the pooled estimate alone.

research_candidates.title: Effects of urban green exercise on mental health: a systematic review and meta-analysis
research_candidates.review_notes: Full open-access publisher article reviewed. The meta-analysis included 15 RCTs with 980 adults and reported an overall mental-health effect favoring urban green exercise (SMD -0.40, 95% CI -0.56 to -0.25; I2 33.9%). Six trials were rated low risk of bias across all RoB 2 domains, eight had some concerns and one was high risk; the authors also note small samples, heterogeneous activity modalities and limited follow-up. Subgroup results by duration, frequency, intensity and sex are useful hypothesis signals but should not be converted into a Brali rule such as '20 minutes is optimal' because subgroup comparisons across a small heterogeneous evidence base do not establish an individual causal dose.

evidence_decisions.source_title: Mental health benefits of urban green—A systematic review and meta-analysis of 56 pre-post control experiments
evidence_decisions.citation_text: Herchet M, Venený M, Kauls L, Mentzel C, Krause T, Surrey C, Hofmann M. People and Nature. 2026. doi:10.1002/pan3.70250.
evidence_decisions.study_design: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of quantitative experimental and quasi-experimental studies with control groups/conditions and pre-post measurements. It synthesised 107 controlled measurements from 56 experiments across eight mental-health and cognitive outcome groups.
evidence_decisions.population: General-population samples across included experiments, with about half of study samples majority university students. Studies were geographically concentrated in Europe and North America; children, older adults and people with illness or disability were underrepresented.
evidence_decisions.intervention_or_exposure: Contact with urban or peri-urban green elements or spaces. The evidence base mixed in-situ exposure with still images, video, VR, window views and sound. Several included in-situ studies compared walking or sitting in greener urban settings with built or less-natural controls.
evidence_decisions.supported_claim: Controlled evidence supports a modest average short-term psychological advantage of urban green exposure over comparison settings for several outcomes. For Brali, this is enough to refine the existing stress-walk protocol: when a genuinely green route is equally convenient, it is reasonable to prefer it. The evidence does not make greenery mandatory and does not establish a specific duration.
unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Green space reliably or immediately reduces stress for every person.
Ten minutes, twenty minutes or another fixed duration is the evidence-based optimum.
The evidence proves a cortisol, parasympathetic or other specific physiological mechanism for this protocol.
Urban green exposure reliably improves working memory.
The pooled effects can be translated into an expected individual percentage improvement.
A short green walk should replace clinical assessment or treatment for persistent or severe anxiety, depression or stress.
limitations: The self-reported stress estimate was heterogeneous: pooled effect 0.40, 95% CI 0.16 to 0.64, with a prediction interval crossing zero; trim-and-fill reduced the estimate to 0.19.
The working-memory pooled effect was not statistically significant.
About half of study samples were majority students, and studies were concentrated in Europe and North America.
The intervention category mixed in-situ urban green with mediated and virtual nature exposure, so pooled estimates are broader than the walking-route use case.
For outcomes where duration was explored, there were no clear signs of a dose-response relationship.
The review focuses mainly on short-term pre-post outcomes and does not establish durable long-term effects.
evidence_decisions.notes: Editorial action: update the existing reviewed stress-walk page rather than create a nature-walk duplicate. Keep the walk low-friction. Present nearby green as a route-choice tie-breaker, not a requirement. Teach the user what to observe after the walk and explicitly reject magic duration, cortisol stories and working-memory overclaiming.

evidence_decisions.source_title: Effects of urban green exercise on mental health: a systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence_decisions.citation_text: Hu G, Luo Q, Zhang P, Zeng H, Ma X. Front Public Health. 2025;13:1677223.
evidence_decisions.study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 15 randomized controlled trials. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and subgroup/meta-regression analyses explored intervention duration, frequency, session duration, intensity and sex.
evidence_decisions.population: 980 adults aged 18 years and older across 15 RCTs of urban green exercise.
evidence_decisions.intervention_or_exposure: Exercise conducted in urban green settings, with heterogeneous activities including walking, cycling and aerobic exercise, compared with varied control conditions.
outcomes: Composite mental-health outcomes across included trials
evidence_decisions.supported_claim: The RCT-only synthesis supports the direction of the Brali refinement: urban green exercise was associated with better mental-health outcomes on average (SMD -0.40, 95% CI -0.56 to -0.25; I2 33.9%). It is supporting evidence for choosing an easy green route when practical, not evidence for a precise Brali dose.
unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Twenty minutes or less is the proven optimal session duration.
One, two or three sessions per week is the proven optimal frequency for an individual.
Low-intensity green exercise is universally superior to other useful physical activity.
The subgroup findings establish a causal sex difference.
The intervention works through GABA, cortisol or a specific neural mechanism.
Short-term study effects establish durable long-term mental-health protection.
limitations: Only 15 RCTs and 980 participants were included.
Activities, populations, control conditions and psychological outcomes varied.
Six studies were low risk of bias across all domains, eight had some concerns and one was high risk.
Many trials were small, and follow-up was generally short.
Subgroup patterns can be hypothesis-generating but do not establish an optimal causal prescription.
evidence_decisions.notes: Use as corroborating evidence only. Do not import the paper's subgroup-derived dosing language into Brali as a hard rule; the stronger editorial value is to support green-route preference while keeping the protocol simple and individualized.
